VII. Comments Received in Response to the Draft Environmental Impact Statement
Environmental Protection Agency - has indicated a lack of objection to the action, but suggests more information be supplied concerning the air quality impacts of the proposed expansion of commercial zones. The text of the final statement contains additional information concerning the impact on air quality.

Department of the Interior - has reviewed the statement in its areas of jurisdiction and expertise and has no comments to offer.

The Port Everglades Authority - urges the Commission to adopt the alternative which would expand the population-mileage formula for cities with physical limitations.
<u>Comment</u>: The draft statement is incorrect in stating that there will be a beneficial environmental effect from a decrease in interlining. It is asserted that there are a number of independent factors which will prevent a decrease in interlining from occurring. (Jones Transfer Company, La Porte Transit, Garment Truckmen Assoc. of New Jersey, Blue and Gray Transportation, Lakeville Motor Express, and A-C Berwick).
Response: The text of the final statement has been modified in order to place the potential benefits of this impact in proper prospective.
<u>Comment</u>: Expansion of the population-mileage formula will encourage urban sprawl. (Lakeville, and Short Haul Survival Committee.)
